title: Restricted scalar-first K-flat tensor models identify derived scalar extensions
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the coefficient universe and let $B\xrightarrow{u}A\xrightarrow{v}S$ be maps of sheaves of commutative rings. Write $\varphi=vu$, and use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], unbounded derived categories and localizations $Q_B,Q_A,Q_S$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Termwise restriction $\operatorname{Res}_v$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms and commutes with the degree-one shift, so it induces $\operatorname{Res}_v:D(S)\to D(A)$ with the canonical comparison
$$\lambda_{v,H}:Q_A(\operatorname{Res}_vH)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_v(Q_SH)$$
for every $S$-complex $H$, compatible with cochain maps and shifts.
Let $G$ represent $K\in D(B)$ via $e:Q_BG\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, and let $f:P\to G$ be any K-flat resolution with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Put $C_S=S\otimes_BP$ with differential $1\otimes d_P$ and $S$ acting on the first factor, and let $F_\varphi=-\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}S$ be derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. There is an $S$-linear cochain isomorphism
$$\tau_S:C_S\xrightarrow{\sim}P\otimes_BS,\qquad s\otimes p\longmapsto p\otimes s,$$
with inverse $p\otimes s\mapsto s\otimes p$. If $c_{\varphi,f}:F_\varphi(Q_BG)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_S(P\otimes_BS)$ is the canonical K-flat computation comparison, then
$$\eta_S=c_{\varphi,f}\circ F_\varphi(e^{-1}):F_\varphi K\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_S(P\otimes_BS)$$
and the composite
$$Q_A(\operatorname{Res}_v C_S)\xrightarrow{Q_A(\operatorname{Res}_v\tau_S)}Q_A(\operatorname{Res}_v(P\otimes_BS))\xrightarrow{\lambda_{v,P\otimes_BS}}\operatorname{Res}_vQ_S(P\otimes_BS)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Res}_v(\eta_S^{-1})}\operatorname{Res}_v(F_\varphi K)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(A)$.
Moreover let $w:A\to T$ be a map to another commutative ring sheaf and let $h:\operatorname{Res}_v S\to\operatorname{Res}_w T$ be any $A$-linear sheaf map; it need not preserve products or units. With the same $P$, the scalar-first and scalar-last maps $h\otimes1_P$ and $1_P\otimes h$ are $A$-linear cochain maps and satisfy
$$\operatorname{Res}_w(\tau_T)\circ(h\otimes1_P)=(1_P\otimes h)\circ\operatorname{Res}_v(\tau_S).$$
Thus, under the displayed derived identifications for $S$ and $T$, localization of $h\otimes1_P$ is precisely the map represented on this resolution by $p\otimes s\mapsto p\otimes h(s)$. No flatness of $u,v,w$, boundedness or completeness is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-coefficient-ordinary-adjunction] to the small ringed site and $v:A\to S$: restriction preserves finite limits and finite colimits, and is additive by [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Thus it preserves kernels, images and cokernels. For a complex $H$, this gives $H^n(\operatorname{Res}_v H)\cong\operatorname{Res}_v H^n(H)$, using the kernel/image description of cohomology in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. In particular a quasi-isomorphism remains a quasi-isomorphism after restriction. This uses no flatness of $v$.

source.place: Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian), kernels and cokernels detected on abelian sheaves; exactness supplied by lem-pur-sheaf-ring-coefficient-ordinary-adjunction.

proof.text: The localization universal property in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], applied to $Q_A\operatorname{Res}_v$, now gives the induced functor and its comparison $\lambda_{v,H}:Q_A(\operatorname{Res}_v H)\cong\operatorname{Res}_v(Q_S H)$. Naturality says $\operatorname{Res}_v(Q_S a)\lambda_{v,H}=\lambda_{v,H'}Q_A(\operatorname{Res}_v a)$ for an $S$-linear cochain map $a:H\to H'$. Restriction leaves the groups, differentials and additive maps unchanged [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]; hence it commutes termwise with $H[1]^n=H^{n+1}$ and the differential $-d_H$. Localizing this identity defines the induced shift comparison. Its compatibility with $\lambda$ follows because both composites are the same termwise identity after precomposition with $Q_S$; uniqueness in the localization universal property gives their equality. This proves precisely the claimed shift compatibility, without asserting that restriction preserves K-flatness.

source.place: Tag 05RU (definition-unbounded-derived-category), localization universal property; shift convention as in def-weil-abstract-derived-category.

proof.text: For each degree $n$ and site object $U$, define $s\otimes p\mapsto p\otimes s$ on the sectionwise tensor over $B(U)$. Additivity and the balancing relation hold: $(\varphi(b)s)\otimes p$ and $s\otimes bp$ both map to $bp\otimes s=p\otimes\varphi(b)s$. The reverse swap obeys the same relations, and both composites are the identity on pure tensors, hence on their sums. Restrictions commute with these formulas. By the tensor construction [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and the sheafification universal property [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], the inverse presheaf maps give inverse sheaf maps. The $S$-action is on the coefficient factor on both sides, so the swap is $S$-linear; this equality also extends uniquely through sheafification. Finally both routes through the differential send $s\otimes p$ to $d_Pp\otimes s$. Thus these maps assemble to the required $S$-linear cochain isomorphism $\tau_S$. The coefficient is in degree zero, so no sign occurs. The identical construction gives $\tau_T$.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sectionwise tensor construction; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), uniqueness of extension to a sheaf.

proof.text: Apply clause (2) of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] to $\varphi=vu$ and the given K-flat resolution $f:P\to G$. Its statement supplies exactly the canonical isomorphism $c_{\varphi,f}:F_\varphi(Q_BG)\cong Q_S(P\otimes_B S)$. Since $e:Q_BG\cong K$, functoriality carries $e^{-1}$ to an isomorphism $F_\varphi K\cong F_\varphi(Q_BG)$. Composing gives exactly $\eta_S=c_{\varphi,f}\circ F_\varphi(e^{-1})$. Apply the same clause to $wu:B\to T$ and the same $f$ to obtain $\eta_T$. The site's smallness ensures that the module categories used here are abelian; all K-flat and flat-term hypotheses are supplied by the item. No property of a scalar restriction of $P$ is used.

source.place: Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), identity underlying topos; Tag 06YT (lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side), K-flat computation as stated in lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings.

proof.text: Write $\delta_S=\operatorname{Res}_v(\eta_S^{-1})\circ\lambda_{v,P\otimes_BS}\circ Q_A(\operatorname{Res}_v\tau_S)$. The first and last maps are functorial images of isomorphisms, and the middle map is the localization comparison from step 2. Their inverse composite, in reverse order, is an inverse to $\delta_S$, by cancellation of each adjacent inverse pair. This is the displayed isomorphism of the statement. Define $\delta_T$ identically with $v,S$ replaced by $w,T$.

source.place: Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change); agent composition of the comparisons in steps 2--4.

proof.text: An $A$-linear $h$ is $B$-linear via $u$, since $h(v(u(b))s)=w(u(b))h(s)$. Consequently the section formulas $s\otimes p\mapsto h(s)\otimes p$ and $p\otimes s\mapsto p\otimes h(s)$ respect the $B$-balancing relations. They are $A$-linear for the coefficient actions, since $h(v(a)s)=w(a)h(s)$. They commute with restrictions and with the differentials $1\otimes d_P$ and $d_P\otimes1$, respectively. The tensor construction and unique sheafification extension [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], with the scalar actions of [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], therefore give the claimed $A$-linear cochain maps. Both composites around the swap square send a pure tensor $s\otimes p$ to $p\otimes h(s)$. The sectionwise maps are equal by additivity and generation by pure tensors, and their sheaf extensions are equal by uniqueness. Thus the square commutes as a square of $A$-complexes. Only additivity and $A$-linearity of $h$ were used.

source.place: Tags 03EK (section-tensor-product) and 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules); agent calculation for an arbitrary A-linear coefficient map.

proof.text:
Set $H_S=P\otimes_BS$, $H_T=P\otimes_BT$, $a=h\otimes1_P$, and $b=1_P\otimes h$, where $b:\operatorname{Res}_vH_S\to\operatorname{Res}_wH_T$ is a map of $A$-complexes. Localizing the square of step 6 and substituting the definitions of $\delta_S,\delta_T$ yields
$$\delta_T Q_A(a)\delta_S^{-1}=\operatorname{Res}_w(\eta_T^{-1})\lambda_{w,H_T}\,Q_A(b)\,\lambda_{v,H_S}^{-1}\operatorname{Res}_v(\eta_S).$$
Indeed $Q_A(\operatorname{Res}_w\tau_T)Q_A(a)=Q_A(b)Q_A(\operatorname{Res}_v\tau_S)$, and the two adjacent copies of $Q_A(\operatorname{Res}_v\tau_S)$ cancel. The right side is exactly the map represented on the chosen scalar-last models by $p\otimes s\mapsto p\otimes h(s)$, with the source and target carried to the displayed derived objects. This uses no alleged $S$-linearity of $h$, and no application of naturality of $\lambda$ to a map between different coefficient categories. It proves the final clause.
